notes: Strong run: the plan is grounded (every file:line citation I spot-checked, roughly 30, resolves to the right text), the prototype experiments back the design, and the only failure is length discipline in the headline (5 sentences vs 3) and approach summary (12 vs 10). Eval critique: check_run.py's section-order check is a false negative here because it substring-matches H3 subheadings ('Step 1. Confirm the open questions', 'Step 4. Tests'); it should match H2 headings only, or it will mis-grade any plan whose steps mention tests or questions. Conversely, nothing mechanical checks the headline/summary sentence bounds even though they are the assertion most likely to fail, so a sentence counter would make that assertion discriminating rather than eyeballed. The 'every assumption carries evidence' assertion passes on presence of citations; it does not catch wrong citations or wrong asides (A3's 'previously 2' clock reads is actually 1), so a spot-check of N citations against the fixture would raise the bar. No assertion checks that experiments ran on a copy rather than in OUTPUT_DIR/repo beyond the final git status, which would miss a prototype that was applied and reverted.
